tasks.short: Read source documents and enter their values into business records.

steps.what: Read source documents and identify values for the required fields.

loop.input: Residual scanned or free-layout documents after structured imports and fixed-template parsing.
loop.output: Typed field values, source locations and explicit unreadable or missing fields.
loop.check: Validate types, required fields, totals and identifiers; preserve source references and route uncertain values to review.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one retry per document; unresolved fields remain blank and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds and fixed templates come first; variable layouts and scans need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Key identified values into draft records in the {ERP}.
Compare draft records with source documents and correct errors before acceptance.
Save the accepted batch in the {ERP} and mark the assignment complete.

tasks.design: Import structured source fields directly into draft records in the {ERP}, removing transcription for those inputs. A bounded extractor handles remaining documents from the {DOCS}; configured validation and a source-linked review screen support clerk acceptance before the {ERP} saves the batch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents varied in layout, and imports lacked consistent mappings or reliable error handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction is available today. AI-assisted coding can shorten mapping, connector and review-screen development.
tasks.still_hard: Poor scans, handwriting, ambiguous identifiers and incorrect originals remain difficult. A matching total does not prove every field is correct.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving conflicting source evidence without inventing values or treating data entry authority as financial approval.

ambition.what: Provide source-linked error reports to teams submitting recurring documents.

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews highlighted fields and recurring source defects instead of transcribing whole documents. The clerk gains authority to return incomplete submissions, subject to an agreed operating policy.

reach.task: Improve the completeness of incoming document submissions.
reach.learn: Required-field standards and clear correction requests.
Field schemas, duplicate prevention and import error handling.

evidence.claim: Doxis extracts fields from invoices, receipts and attachments.
Rossum documents invoice extraction, validation and ERP integration in the Fugro case.
The proposed effort reduction for mixed data entry documents requires local measurement.

assumptions: The representative batch contains financial or operational records entered into the {ERP}.
Acceptance here confirms transcription accuracy; payment and substantive transaction approvals belong to downstream roles.
Existing imports or extraction configuration are reused before custom development.
Estimates cover one document family and destination. GDPR controls apply; EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual use.
unknowns: Document volumes, languages, scan quality and handwriting frequency.
Whether structured submissions can replace documents at source.
Whether the {ERP} supports draft imports and safe retries.
Which fields require mandatory review and who can accept records.
Data processing permissions and consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: What field-level error and referral rates occur on representative documents, including poor scans?
new_work: Review uncertain values and critical fields.
Maintain mappings, validation rules and representative evaluation samples.
Monitor duplicate imports, rejected records and extraction drift.
Give submitting teams source-linked correction reports.
tasks.statement: Read source documents such as canceled checks, sales reports, or bills, and enter data in specific data fields or onto tapes or disks for subsequent entry, using keyboards or scanners.

tasks.short: Collect incoming data, organise it into entry batches, and check completeness and accuracy.

steps.what: Collect source documents and files from the {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.
Sort documents by record type, reference, and processing priority.
Read source values and check required fields, references, dates, and totals.

loop.input: Residual PDFs and scanned forms; structured source files bypass the model.
loop.output: Typed fields, source locations, unreadable-field flags, and missing-data flags.
loop.check: Validate schema, required fields, totals, duplicates, and reference matches. A clerk reviews document-derived values before release.
loop.stop: One extraction and at most one targeted retry per document; unresolved fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports and fixed templates cover regular inputs; variable layouts and free text remain.

steps.what: Clarify missing or contradictory information with the source owner through {EMAIL}.
Assemble the checked entry batch and record its readiness in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Prefer structured intake through the {WORKFLOW} and direct imports into the {ERP}, removing document preparation where possible. A bounded extractor handles remaining documents from the {DOCS}; deterministic checks build a prepared entry batch and attach precise questions for human clarification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable documents and scattered intake channels made one import format insufficient.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms and file parsers cover regular submissions. Document extraction can supply draft fields for the remainder, with bounded retries and explicit review.
tasks.still_hard: An extractor cannot establish facts missing from the source. Poor scans, inconsistent references, and source-owner response times remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a useful clarification question and recognise when a complete-looking submission is substantively wrong.

ambition.what: Submission-readiness feedback for occasional internal requesters

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews document-derived fields and helps requesters fix incomplete submissions. With agreed acceptance criteria, they can return incomplete batches before entry rather than chase errors downstream.

reach.task: Help internal requesters submit complete operational records
reach.learn: Design clear intake questions, explain rejected fields, and identify avoidable submission friction.

evidence.claim: Doxis reads invoices, receipts, and attachments into fields; support for other document types needs testing.
PostNL offers business-post digitisation that turns forms into data.
Fugro's documented invoice case shows extraction and validation operating at scale; its results are not a forecast for this workload.
Time shares, review effort, and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: Intake includes both structured files and documents; their exact proportions are unconfirmed.
Sorting uses supplied identifiers and known document types; unidentified items enter an exception queue.
Source owners are internal colleagues.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on intended use, with consultation assessed under national rules.
unknowns: What are the document types, languages, scan quality, and monthly volumes?
Which senders can switch to structured submissions?
What personal data, processing locations, and retention limits apply?
Who may approve access and processing arrangements?
research_questions: Which source families can bypass extraction entirely?
How accurately can required fields be extracted on a representative, held-out sample?
Which clarification requests can be avoided by changing intake questions?
new_work: Review extracted values with source evidence.
Handle unreadable and unidentified submissions.
Maintain schemas, reference lists, and intake instructions.
Monitor extraction quality when document layouts change.
tasks.statement: Compile, sort, and verify the accuracy of data before it is entered.

tasks.short: Compare entered records with their sources and resolve verification discrepancies.

steps.what: Match entered records in the {ERP} to their source documents.
Compare identifiers, amounts, dates, and text against the source documents.

loop.input: Original documents without structured source data, withheld from entered values during extraction.
loop.output: Source values with locations and uncertainty flags for deterministic comparison.
loop.check: Compare exact values, approved normalisations, totals, and reference data. Document-derived agreement alone cannot certify critical fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one targeted retry maximum; unreadable, conflicting, and critical document fields require source review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact comparison handles structured originals; variable document layouts require reading before comparison.

steps.what: Re-enter selected fields in the {ERP} verification screen where double entry is used.
Resolve verification discrepancies and decide whether records pass the source check.
Record verification status and refer failed records for correction in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: An integration links records in the {ERP} to original evidence in the {DOCS}, compares structured originals directly, and extracts comparison values from residual documents. Replace routine double entry with validated comparisons where the control owner accepts the replacement; people review discrepancies, critical document fields, and a sample of apparent matches before the {WORKFLOW} records outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Double entry was an accessible control when sources were unstructured and record-to-document links were weak.
tasks.enabler_now: Source links, deterministic field comparison, and bounded extraction can concentrate human checking on uncertain evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Two readings can share the same error. The control must detect omitted records, wrong source matches, and plausible but incorrect extraction.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real mismatch from a legitimate format difference and challenge misleading agreement.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time repeating values and more time inspecting uncertain or consequential fields. Verification authority does not expand automatically.

reach.learn: Use risk-based sampling, measure false acceptance, and evaluate control independence.

evidence.claim: Exact source comparison and exception routing are deterministic when authoritative structured originals exist.
Rossum provides invoice extraction and validation; this does not establish equivalence to a customer's double-entry control.
The reported spreadsheet row-limit incident illustrates why verification must include record counts and completeness.
Remaining effort and build ranges assume source review remains for critical document fields.

assumptions: Entry itself happens outside this task, after preparation of the entry batch.
The illustrated workload includes double entry for selected fields.
Elimination of double entry requires acceptance of the replacement control; mandatory checks remain until that acceptance.
Correcting failed records belongs to the connected correction task.
unknowns: Which fields require double entry, independent checking, or full source review?
Who can approve a change to the verification control?
Are original files immutable and reliably linked to records?
What false-acceptance rate and sampling plan are acceptable?
research_questions: Does the replacement detect known errors, omissions, and wrong-document matches?
Does extraction agree incorrectly with entered values on difficult documents?
Can batch counts and totals be reconciled end to end?
new_work: Review uncertain and critical source fields.
Sample apparent matches for silent errors.
Maintain comparison tolerances and field mappings.
Retest controls after source or system changes.
tasks.statement: Compare data with source documents, or re-enter data in verification format to detect errors.

tasks.short: File completed documents, maintain record links, and store required paper originals.

steps.what: Identify completed records and their final documents in the {ERP}.
Choose the filing category, destination, and access class from document metadata.
Resolve uncertain categories, access restrictions, or retention requirements.
Name and save final documents in the correct {DOCS} location.
Update the filing register in the {SPREADSHEET} with document locations.
Place required paper originals in labelled folders and secure storage.

tasks.design: Configure completion triggers, naming, metadata, and access inheritance in the {DOCS}, using the {WORKFLOW} only where cross-system routing is needed. Replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} register with searchable record links; unresolved filing categories go to the records owner, while required paper originals remain physically filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion status, filing metadata, and document storage were disconnected. A separate register compensated for weak search and record links.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document rules can handle known categories. Small integrations can carry completion status and identifiers without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Retention ambiguity, legal holds, legacy permissions, and physical originals remain. GDPR and applicable national records rules constrain storage and access.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an exceptional record whose sensitivity, retention, or evidential value differs from its usual category.
tasks.altitude: Routine digital filing largely disappears, while physical storage and exceptional classification remain. With delegated retrieval access, the clerk can assemble complete case packs; retention and access-policy decisions remain with the records owner.

reach.task: Retrieve complete records for authorised requests
reach.learn: Use record indexes, check access rights, and identify missing or superseded documents.

evidence.claim: Metadata-driven filing, naming, access inheritance, and searchable indexes are established document-management capabilities.
Digital filing can be mostly configured even when physical storage remains manual.
Time shares and build ranges assume known filing categories and an existing document store.

assumptions: The illustrative workload mixes digital filing with required paper originals.
Reliable record metadata is available for routine filing; unmatched items remain restricted pending review.
The separate filing register duplicates information that the {DOCS} can hold.
No automatic destruction or retention-period changes are included.
The large routine digital portion supports more automation than the supplied human-task prior suggests.
unknowns: What proportion of filing effort concerns paper originals?
Are retention schedules, access classes, and legal holds documented?
Can the {DOCS} provide the register's search and reporting functions?
Which records require original paper under applicable national rules?
Do access changes or employee monitoring trigger consultation requirements?
research_questions: Can known metadata classify a representative filing sample without inspecting content?
Do inherited permissions prevent unauthorised retrieval?
Can users retrieve a complete case without the separate register?
new_work: Resolve unmatched filing categories.
Maintain metadata mappings and filing rules.
Check broken links, duplicates, and access inheritance.
Test retrieval completeness and retain physical-location references.
tasks.statement: Store completed documents in appropriate locations.

tasks.short: Find entry errors, correct routine mistakes, and refer disputed changes to a supervisor.

steps.what: Find invalid, duplicate, or inconsistent records in the {ERP}.
Retrieve source documents and establish the correct values.
Apply clear corrections to records in the {ERP}.
Send unresolved discrepancies and supporting evidence to the supervisor through {EMAIL}.
Discuss conflicting evidence and approve, reject, or defer the proposed correction.
Record the decision and apply approved changes in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure validation in the {ERP}; use a small integration to attach source evidence from the {DOCS} and populate an exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Apply only allowlisted corrections backed by an authoritative value, with before-and-after logs and rollback; disputed or consequential changes require a supervisor decision before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source evidence was separate from records, and correction permissions were too broad for unattended updates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation and import interfaces can be connected cheaply. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort without replacing correction rules.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting sources, stale master data, and changes affecting payments or legal records need accountable decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently valid correction changes business meaning or hides an upstream mistake.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of recurring entry-error causes

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time finding evidence and posting corrections. With delegated authority, they can prioritise recurring error causes for the operations supervisor; approval rights for consequential changes stay with that supervisor.

reach.learn: Group errors by source, measure recurrence, and distinguish symptoms from causes.

evidence.claim: Validation rules, evidence links, and controlled updates can handle routine structured-data corrections.
Rossum documents invoice extraction, validation, and ERP posting; this supports feasibility for invoices, not every record type.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates requiring customer validation.

assumptions: The main workload is operational records in the {ERP}; equivalent flows may use the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Automatic corrections exclude bank details, payment instructions, and other consequential fields.
Step shares represent combined task effort across the clerk and supervisor.
unknowns: Which system and source are authoritative for each field?
Which corrections may run without individual approval?
Are record versions, update interfaces, and rollback available?
Does employee consultation apply under national rules or existing agreements?
research_questions: Which error categories have unambiguous correction rules?
What proportion of referrals involve conflicting evidence rather than missing links?
new_work: Review unresolved evidence and failed updates.
Maintain correction allowlists and source precedence.
Sample automatic changes and test rollback.
Review recurring error causes with source owners.
tasks.statement: Locate and correct data entry errors, or report them to supervisors.

tasks.short: Record completed batches, activity details and unresolved work in an operational log.

steps.what: Read completion details and batch counts from the {ERP}.
Copy batch identifiers, counts and status into the shared log in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Reconcile logged totals against completed batches and explain discrepancies.

tasks.design: Capture completion events from the {ERP} and configure an append-only activity register in the {WORKFLOW}, replacing the shared {SPREADSHEET}. Deterministic reconciliation compares expected and completed batches; a {BI} view highlights gaps, and the clerk approves discrepancy explanations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completion events were inaccessible or inconsistent across systems. A shared workbook provided a cheap manual bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Exports and event interfaces can supply the log. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of small connectors and reconciliation views.
tasks.still_hard: Work done outside connected systems can remain invisible. Retries, partial batches and reopened assignments need explicit status rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining whether a discrepancy reflects missing work, a system fault or a legitimate processing exception.

ambition.what: Reprioritise unresolved batches each morning using reconciled backlog counts.

tasks.altitude: The clerk stops copying counts and investigates missing or inconsistent events. The clerk can propose the next batch order; the operations supervisor retains staffing and service-priority decisions.

reach.task: Identify recurring delays between document receipt and record acceptance.
reach.learn: Event definitions, reconciliation and process measures.

evidence.claim: Event capture, append-only registers and count reconciliation are deterministic capabilities.
The documented spreadsheet row-limit failure supports checking capacity and completeness in operational logging.
In the Netherlands, worker-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent.

assumptions: A shared workbook bridges the operational system and team reporting in this representative setting.
Existing native logs are assessed before adding a register.
The proposed view measures batches and exceptions; individual productivity monitoring requires separate assessment.
GDPR applies to identifiable activity records. National rules determine employee consultation and monitoring requirements.
unknowns: Whether a native activity register already meets the need.
Which completion events and historical records can be accessed.
Whether current logs support payroll, billing or formal audit evidence.
Retention periods, access roles and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which reconciliation rules detect missing events without treating retries as additional completed work?
new_work: Investigate missing events and duplicate identifiers.
Maintain status definitions and reconciliation rules.
Approve explanatory corrections while preserving original events.
Review access, retention and reporting changes.
tasks.statement: Maintain logs of activities and completed work.

tasks.short: Select source documents and reference materials for each data entry assignment.

steps.what: Read the assignment and identify required records in the {ERP}.
Retrieve source documents and reference lists from the {DOCS}.
Check document relevance, versions and completeness before releasing the source pack.

loop.input: Documents whose type or relevance cannot be established from identifiers and metadata.
loop.output: Proposed document matches with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Check assignment identifiers, required document types and versions; the clerk approves the selected pack.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one retry per ambiguous document; unresolved items enter the missing material list.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle indexed documents; inconsistent headings and free text require limited interpretation.

tasks.design: Configure assignment requirements in the {ERP}; an integration retrieves matching documents from the {DOCS}. A bounded classifier handles ambiguous documents, and a {WORKFLOW} screen presents the proposed source pack and gaps for clerk approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments, document identifiers and versions were held separately. Manual retrieval was cheaper than maintaining bespoke links.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata and document interfaces support matching. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors and a small review screen.
tasks.still_hard: Missing originals, unreliable version labels and access restrictions still prevent complete packs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that a plausible document belongs to the wrong transaction, and finding the responsible document owner.

ambition.what: Check source readiness before each scheduled processing batch.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time retrieving files and more time resolving incomplete assignments. The clerk can return an unready pack with a precise missing material list; transaction approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Improve document indexing for recurring source packs.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, version control and retention categories.

evidence.claim: Identifier matching and completeness rules can assemble recurring source packs without an autonomous agent.
Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files, supporting document organisation feasibility.

assumptions: The representative setting uses recurring finance or operations assignments with documents in the {DOCS}.
Time shares and remaining effort are design estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Estimates cover one assignment family. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed; national rules govern any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether assignments contain stable document identifiers.
Whether reference lists and document versions are authoritative.
Which read permissions and interfaces are available.
Whether the proposed work allocation changes require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: How accurately can metadata matching select documents before any model classification is needed?
new_work: Review proposed source packs and unresolved gaps.
Maintain assignment requirements and document matching rules.
Investigate missing documents and broken access links.
tasks.statement: Select materials needed to complete work assignments.

tasks.short: Prepare and load paper or specialist media into office equipment.

steps.what: Read the job ticket in the {DOCS} and identify required media and settings.
Select and load the required media into {OTHER} office equipment.
Inspect the first feed or output sample from {OTHER} office equipment.

tasks.design: Configure media requirements and setup instructions in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to job tickets in the {DOCS}. Use digital delivery where the recipient and process permit it, eliminating those loading jobs; retained physical jobs still require a person to load and inspect {OTHER} office equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loading and checking media require physical handling. Software alone cannot perform those actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured job tickets can reduce preparation effort, and digital delivery can remove some jobs. There is no assumed breakthrough in physical loading.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist media, accessibility requirements, jams and first-sample quality checks remain physical work.
tasks.human_edge: Handling unusual media and noticing feed, alignment or tactile defects before a full run.
tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter, but the clerk's physical duties and decision rights largely stay unchanged. Any larger reduction depends on eliminating eligible physical jobs.

reach.task: Assess which recurring output jobs can use digital delivery.
reach.learn: Recipient requirements, accessibility needs and equipment costs.

evidence.claim: Job-ticket configuration can simplify preparation, while physical loading still requires a person.
Digital substitution can eliminate eligible media-handling jobs, subject to recipient and process requirements.

assumptions: Paper is the typical medium; removable or specialist media occur only where the operation requires them.
Step shares describe physical jobs that remain. Possible digital substitution is not counted in their remaining effort.
The estimate covers job-ticket configuration, without equipment replacement.
Access and consultation estimates assume no new worker monitoring; national rules may change the required process.
unknowns: Which equipment and media are actually used.
Which recipients require physical or accessible output.
Whether digital delivery is already available and authorised.
How often loading faults and media changes occur.
research_questions: Which recurring physical jobs can be eliminated while meeting recipient and accessibility requirements?
new_work: Maintain media specifications and setup instructions.
Confirm digital delivery requirements for eligible job types.
Keep equipment fault and media compatibility information current.
tasks.statement: Load machines with required input or output media, such as paper, cards, disks, tape, or Braille media.

tasks.short: Recover unreadable messages using source checks, approved decoding procedures, and sender clarification.

steps.what: Open the unreadable message and retain its original in the {DOCS}.
Inspect characters, file properties, and source copies to identify the likely fault.
Apply approved decoding or decryption procedures using the secure utility in {OTHER}.
Compare uncertain fragments with source context and mark gaps without inventing missing content.
Ask the sender for a clean copy or confirmation of unresolved fragments through {EMAIL}.
Check the recovered message against authoritative evidence and approve it for use.
Save the verified message and its recovery history in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure a recovery queue in the {WORKFLOW}, retaining originals in the {DOCS}; remove recurring faults through upstream format validation. Deterministic routines on the {DATA_PLATFORM} diagnose known encoding faults and invoke an approved secure decoding utility in {OTHER}, accepting results only when format, integrity, and source checks pass. People resolve ambiguous fragments, approve clarification requests through the {EMAIL}, and approve recovered messages before the {WORKFLOW} releases them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery was infrequent and spread across file formats, source copies, and restricted utilities. The cost of connecting these tools outweighed the clerical time saved.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building format checks, adapters, and comparison views. Existing decoding procedures remain the technical basis; no cryptographic breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Missing source data and unavailable keys cannot be repaired by inference. Genuine cryptographic faults need an authorised technical specialist. GDPR requires lawful access, data minimisation, and retention controls; assess EU AI Act obligations if a model is later introduced.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when plausible text lacks evidence, obtain authoritative clarification, and decide when the message must remain unresolved.

ambition.what: A shared unreadable-message recovery queue for office clerks.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated decoding attempts to difficult recoveries and recurring source faults. The keyer gains delegated authority to request clean copies and route technical failures; authority over the message's business meaning does not expand.

reach.task: Locate authoritative originals and maintain document provenance.
reach.learn: Version history, retention rules, and evidence linking recovered text to its source.

reach.task: Diagnose recurring message-format failures between systems.
reach.learn: Character encodings, file signatures, integrity checks, and secure escalation procedures.

evidence.claim: Known encoding faults and authorised decryption procedures can use deterministic routines; missing keys or content require escalation.
PostNL offers document digitisation and form-to-data services, supporting source intake rather than cryptographic recovery.
The proposed workflow, time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are estimates rather than a documented implementation.

assumptions: This supplemental duty is uncommon in a mid-size company; most cases concern damaged files or encoding faults.
The steps describe active handling time. Sender waiting time is excluded, and clarification occurs only when needed.
Genuine cryptographic cases use existing authorised procedures and keys; technical ownership sits with a specialist.
Automated diagnosis may return unknown and route the case without attempting speculative recovery.
Build ranges cover a small set of common formats and one secure utility.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it; no individual productivity monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Whether this duty occurs and whether messages are encrypted, misencoded, damaged, or visually illegible.
Case volumes, common formats, active handling times, and error consequences.
Availability of authoritative source copies, approved procedures, keys, and utility interfaces.
Who may approve recovered content and contact senders.
Applicable national consultation rules, employee representation arrangements, and access lead times.
research_questions: Which recurring faults can be eliminated by validating the source format?
Which integrity and source checks reliably distinguish a correct recovery from merely readable text?
Does a sample of past cases support deterministic recovery before specialist escalation?
new_work: Review unresolved fragments and approve clarification requests.
Maintain the approved format and recovery-procedure list.
Investigate failed integrity checks and recurring source faults.
Test adapters when file formats or secure utilities change.
Maintain access permissions, retention settings, and recovery logs.
tasks.statement: Resolve garbled or indecipherable messages, using cryptographic procedures and equipment.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts from repeated keying checks and filing towards source clarification, exception resolution, and evidence-based quality control. Broader acceptance or improvement decisions require explicit delegation; consequential corrections and retention decisions remain with accountable owners.
reach: Management analyst: investigate recurring intake and entry defects.
Quality control systems manager: assess verification controls and sampling.
File clerk: provide complete, authorised record retrieval.
skills_to_grow: Field schemas, validation rules, and source precedence
Clear questions for missing or contradictory source data
Document metadata, retention, and access control
Exception analysis and controlled process improvement
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a data-quality coordinator who helps occasional requesters submit usable records, investigates recurring defects, and proposes measurable control improvements across intake, verification, correction, and filing.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward source quality, exception resolution and reliable batch completion. Clerks can gain defined rights to return incomplete submissions and accept verified transcriptions; financial approvals and staffing decisions remain with their existing owners.
reach: File clerk: improve source indexing and version control.
Computer systems analyst: specify field mappings and reliable imports.
Management analyst: investigate recurring processing delays.
Administrative services manager: assess digital substitution for physical output.
skills_to_grow: Clear correction requests and exception escalation.
Basic workflow configuration and access controls.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a shared source-quality service that returns precise correction requests, tracks recurring submission defects and helps adjacent teams prevent them.

role_batches.altitude: The role spends less time operating recovery tools and more time establishing whether recovered information is trustworthy. Business approval rights remain with the relevant record owner.
reach: Document provenance work with file clerks.
Recurring interface-fault diagnosis with computer systems analysts.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become the office's message-recovery coordinator, offering a shared queue and using recurring faults to improve source submissions.
